findings.reason: the endpoint is reached by routing the two `cached_stream_events` callers through `_summarised_observation` (or by lifting the events cache's byte-eviction veto on the summary path), and a plan that instead builds a resume store inside `_PARSED_STREAMS` sends a node to reimplement `_StreamSummary`.
findings.text: s88's premise that the parsed-stream cache must newly "keep each stream's resume state (identity, offset and parsed summary) for every live stream, bounded by the number of live runs rather than by bytes" ignores that `_stream_summary` and its `_STREAM_SUMMARIES` map (`:3735`, `_STREAM_SUMMARY_LIMIT = 2048` at `:3736`) are exactly that: a count-bounded, per-path summary holding `dev/ino/size/mtime_ns`, `offset`, `head`, folds and bounds, which returns `[], 0, False` without touching bytes when the identity is unmoved (`:3880`-`:3884`) and re-reads only from `stored.offset` when the stream grew (`:3890`-`:3895`); `_summarised_observation` (`:3966`) already front-routes `observe_stream`, and `observe_stream`'s own resume branch (`:4463`-`:4483`) already re-parses from a carried offset when the events cache has no entry — so the 42.7% is the two callers that bypass this path (`reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1197`, `reckon/crew/recovery_stream.py:837`, both on `cached_stream_events`), not a missing resume store, and adding resume state to `_PARSED_STREAMS` is work the file already did

findings.reason: a fourth copy of the identity/offset pair drifts from `_stream_summary`'s eviction rule, and the section should name `_STREAM_SUMMARIES` as the owner to extend or explicitly delete one of the three.
findings.text: the census of per-stream identity-and-offset encodings in `reckon/_backends.py` is `_PARSED_STREAMS` with `_ParsedStream.identity` (`:3651`, `:3637`) and its `grows` branch seeking `prior_identity[2]` (`:3678`-`:3691`), `_STREAM_SUMMARIES` with `_StreamSummary.identity`/`offset` bounded by count (`:3735`, `:3736`, `:3768`/`:3776`), and the caller-carried resume shape `{"state","offset","head"}` published at `:4483` (`obs.stream_state["offset"] = _last_line_boundary(path)`) and consumed at `:4463`-`:4483`; s88's "keeps each stream's resume state (identity, offset and parsed summary)" makes a fourth, forked from `_STREAM_SUMMARIES`, whose eviction rule and growth check are already the ones the section's Done-when asserts

findings.reason: naming the un-memoised twin and the head-keyed answer store turns s87's open-ended discovery into a named owner to extend, and rules out the per-site third memo the current wording would allow.
findings.text: s87 leaves the offending read to be discovered ("the module that makes the call (to be named in the manifest)") but the census of git subprocesses on the station's own path is small and the memo that answers them already exists: `_commits_beyond_base` (`:525`) reads the worktree revision off the git directory as files and answers from `_COMMITS_BEYOND_BASE_CACHE` keyed `(worktree, base) → (head, count)` and from the on-disk count answer store (`_stored_count_answer`/`_remember_count_answer`, `:558`-`:576`), while its sibling `_worktree_diff_paths` (`:578`-`:605`) runs two git subprocesses (`:587`, `:593`) over the same worktree with no head key at all, and is reached from the same recovery record path (`:655`); the answer store itself (`_git_answer_tree_path`, `:163`) and `file_memo.memoized` (`:231`, `:429`) are the other existing owners a fix must extend

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each section asks for one behaviour behind one surface (s88 one cache's resume semantics, s87 one read answered from a memo); neither proposes a fan of helpers over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — s88's resume state would be the third per-stream encoding of identity and offset in `reckon/_backends.py`, beside `_PARSED_STREAMS` (`:3651`/`:3656`) and the count-bounded `_STREAM_SUMMARIES` (`:3735`), whose owner is `_stream_summary`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 2958, cli_options 527, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25: s87 and s88 add no CLI option, MCP view or operator-facing refusal family; s88's additions are one cache-resume behaviour, one test file and the node fragment, and it retires the whole-population re-parse that the byte-bounded eviction causes, so there is no new surface to account for.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — s88 asks `_PARSED_STREAMS` to grow a per-stream resume state (identity, offset, parsed summary) bounded by live-run count, which `reckon/_backends.py:3860` `_stream_summary` with `_STREAM_SUMMARIES`/`_STREAM_SUMMARY_LIMIT = 2048` (`:3735`, `:3736`) already is, front-routed for every observation by `_summarised_observation` (`:3966`); s87's per-tick git call has a head-keyed answer store to extend at `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:525`.
